transcript:
Header: 2026-03-11 10:30 AM PT | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Sara Patel (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Tom Becker (BridgeRiver - Head Security), Anita Desai (BridgeRiver - Platform), Rajiv Menon (BridgeRiver - CTO), Leah Chang (BridgeRiver - Compliance)

00:00 Sara: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC security sync, um we'll go through the open items from last week - SSO, audit logs, SOC 2 artifacts, and pen test scope. Miguel is here for the deep tech bits.
00:12 Tom: Yep, thanks Sara. Quick note we're on a tight timeline, we'd like to have compliance sign-off for the pilot by end of month, so any blockers on docs or access will slow us down.
00:20 Miguel: Got it. I'll run through what we have on SSO and logs, and then we can toggle to the data retention questions.
00:29 Anita: Quick ask — for the dedicated pool, will we get full host-level logs or just request-level traces? We need to forward to our SIEM (Splunk).
00:38 Miguel: Right now Redwood exposes request-level audit logs with auth context, model, route, token counts, etc. We can also enable expanded runtime logs in the private deployment; for hosted/dedicated there's a JSON audit log payload we can stream to your syslog/Splunk forwarder. I'll send a sample.
00:55 Leah: What's included in the audit log schema? Do we get user_id, request_id, response_status, and redaction for user content? We need to ensure PII isn't in the logs.
01:05 Miguel: The schema includes request_id, timestamp, route, client_id, model_id, latency_ms, token_counts, and optionally an obfuscated prompt hash. We intentionally don't include full prompt by default for hosted, but for private you can enable full payload logging if your retention/policy permits. There is a content redaction feature (auto PII scrubbing) but it's an opt-in and we recommend verifying with your compliance team.
01:28 Tom: That helps. For the pilot we prefer no prompt text in the logs; just hashes, and we want logs forwarded to our SIEM with a 180-day retention. Is that doable?
01:38 Miguel: Yes, we can configure outbound log forwarding. Retention on Redwood side for hosted is configurable up to 90 days by default on the pilot plan; for 180 days we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment. We'll note that as an ask.
01:52 Sara: Action: Miguel will send sample JSON audit log and Splunk ingestion instructions.
02:00 Rajiv: On SSO, we've run into an issue importing the SAML metadata you shared; some of the attribute mappings are unclear. Can Miguel walk through the SP metadata and the assertion attributes Redwood expects?
02:12 Miguel: Sure. Redwood expects NameID or email as the primary subject, then optional attributes: groups, role, org_id. We also support IdP-initiated flows. I'll attach an SP metadata example and a sample assertion payload; apologies if last week's file used an older field name — sometimes our export tool labels it RedwoodAPI vs Redwood-Infer.
02:35 Anita: We tried the SSO test and we saw a 401, likely mapping issue. Also question: do you support SCIM for provisioning?
02:44 Miguel: We do support SCIM for user provisioning in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports SAML SSO for auth; provisioning via Okta or G-suite SCIM is available with enterprise plan. For the pilot if you want SCIM we can demo it but might be scoped to the Dedicated trial.
03:00 Leah: SOC 2 — last week you mentioned a SOC 2 Type II completed Q4 2025. We need the report and the controls matrix.
03:09 Sara: Yes, we'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and the controls matrix. Note some items in the full report are redacted for third-party distribution; we'll provide a compliance pack and a redacted report for your review.
03:20 Tom: Also, pen test — we want to run a pen test against the dedicated pool. Is Redwood okay with us running tests? Any guardrails?
03:29 Miguel: We allow customer-led pen tests but we require a scope and scheduler. For hosted shared infra we limit tests; Dedicated/private are fine with a pre-approved scope. We'll need a notice window and an approved vendor list. We'll share the standard pen-test policy.
03:43 Rajiv: On encryption: we need to ensure keys are customer-managed KMS/HSM and that model cache isn't persisted to disk in plaintext. Can you confirm?
03:52 Miguel: For Private deployments you can plug in your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM). For Dedicated, we offer integration with customer KMS via key wrapping and envelope encryption — we'll share architecture notes. The KV cache is in-memory and encrypted at rest on disk with customer-managed keys in private/deidicated configs; for hosted we manage keys by default but offer BYOK for enterprise customers.
04:20 Anita: Do you have audit logs for admin actions (who changed routes, who changed rollback policies)? That's critical for our change control.
04:28 Miguel: Yes, admin audit logs are separate and include user actions: rollout, model pinning, scaling operations. Those can be forwarded to your SIEM. We'll include the fields mapping.
04:40 Leah: Data residency question: our production data must stay in Canada for some lines of business. Are you able to pin region for the Dedicated pool?
04:49 Sara: Yes, we offer region pinning for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can run in us-west, eu-west regions today; Canada regions are available via private deployments or partner cloud — we'll escalate to the infra team for specifics.
05:05 Tom: Okay sounds good. One minor note — you mentioned an auto-redaction feature, can you elaborate on false positives/negatives? Compliance will want to see how it works.
05:16 Miguel: The auto-redaction uses regex and heuristics; it's not perfect. We run it as a first pass and provide a manual review option in the console for flagged items. For pilot we can run a sample dataset against the redaction tool and show results.
05:35 Sara: Recap: Miguel to send SAML metadata + sample assertion + audit log JSON; Sara to send SOC2 pack + pen-test policy; BridgeRiver to confirm retention and pen-test vendor. We'll aim to have the benchmark scheduled week of 3/22.
05:50 Tom: Thanks. Any outstanding blockers? From our side it's mainly confirmation of the 180-day retention and SAML attribute mapping. If those are confirmed we can proceed.
06:00 Anita: Also please include the Splunk HEC endpoint example for log forwarding, that will speed our infra work.
06:08 Miguel: Will do. I'll include an example HEC configuration and a small FluentD config snippet.
06:18 Leah: On the SOC2 pack, please include the mapping between Redwood controls and our control framework; that helps accelerate the review.
06:26 Sara: We'll map the controls matrix to your framework and include it in the pack.
06:33 Rajiv: One more ops question — if we do dedicated, what's the expected lead time to spin up a regional pool? We need a cost/lead time number for planning.
06:42 Sara: Typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for a Dedicated regional pool depending on capacity; we'll include the expected timeline and cost estimate in the pricing doc.
06:50 Tom: Great. If there's nothing else we can wrap. Thanks everyone.
06:55 Sara: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.

Notes: transcription contains a few mis-hearings (e.g., Redwood product labels inconsistent), filler words, and occasional speaker label ambiguity consistent with auto-generated transcripts.
